decisions.evidence: Maker r1: “Save a bookmark … paste a URL”; client r1: “This is sufficient for the first version.” Maker r4 reports the save flow implemented and client r4 accepts it.
decisions.note: The presented URL-saving behavior conforms to the reference. Recorded once across specification and implementation stages.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1 enumerates save fields as “URL, optional title/notes” and separately defers automatic details; maker r3 again lists “save (url/title/notes).” Client r1 mentions deferring automatic details but does not identify the missing editable description behavior.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the enumerated bookmark fields omit description, so the required before/after editing of collected title and description is incomplete. The client did not surface that separate difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1 presents “Edit & delete — correct details,” within a model enumerated as URL/title/notes and tags; maker r3 lists only generic “edit.” Client r1 and r3 approve without mentioning the omitted description field.
decisions.note: The scoped edit behavior lacks the reference-required description field. This remained unexpressed through the specification and task gates.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1: “delete with a confirmation step”; maker r4 reports delete implemented. Client r4 explicitly accepts the delete behavior.
decisions.note: Deletion, with an additional confirmation safeguard, conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1: “click to open in a new tab”; maker r3: “SC-002 open exact url”; client r4 accepts the browse/open behavior.
decisions.note: Opening the original URL in a new tab is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1 proposes organizing with tags; maker r3 maps “tags + filter” to tasks; maker r4 reports tagging implemented. Client r4 accepts tagging.
decisions.note: The recorded ability to assign tags conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1: “group/filter with tags”; maker r3 lists “tags + filter”; client r4 accepts tagging behavior.
decisions.note: Filtering bookmarks by a selected tag conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1: “Auto-fetch titles/favicons — Nice-to-have, not required”; client r1: “I’m happy to defer automatic page details.” Maker r4 confirms “no auto-fetched titles/favicons.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client explicitly identifies automatic page details and accepts their deferral. This is one lifecycle decision carried into implementation.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1 describes browse as only “see all saved bookmarks” while enumerating no description field and making fetched favicons non-required; client r1 does not discuss the required per-item description/favicon presentation. Maker r4 broadly reports browse implemented, and client r4 broadly accepts it.
decisions.note: The presented model cannot expose all required list fields—particularly description and target favicon—per item. Neither approval surfaces this display-level difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1: “Import/export from other browsers — Out of scope for v1”; client r1: “I’m happy to defer … import/export.” Maker r4 confirms import remains excluded.
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies import and accepts its deferral at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1: “Import/export from other browsers — Out of scope for v1”; client r1: “I’m happy to defer … import/export.” Maker r4 confirms export remains excluded.
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies export and accepts its deferral at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker r2: “saving a URL you already have will warn but still let you save it deliberately”; client r2 responds only, “The plan sounds good.” Maker r4 reports duplicate-warning tests, and client r4 gives broad final acceptance without identifying duplicate creation.
decisions.note: The plan permits duplicates instead of converging on editing the existing bookmark. Neither the plan-gate nor implementation-review response surfaces that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker r2 specifies: “Search covers title, address, notes, and tags,” omitting description; client r2 says only “The plan sounds good.” Maker r3 repeats “FR-011 keyword search,” and client r3 approves.
decisions.note: The explicitly enumerated full-text scope omits description, so it does not fulfill the required title/description/note/URL search. The difference passed unexpressed at plan and task gates.

decisions.evidence: Maker r1 offers only “search by keyword”; maker r2 describes field-based search; maker r3’s exhaustive requirement map again lists only “keyword search” and a separate tag filter. Clients r1–r3 approve without requesting `#tag`, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, or quoted-phrase matching.
decisions.note: Across the specification, plan, and exhaustive task map, search is defined as simple keyword matching rather than the reference query syntax. The client never surfaces these differences.

decisions.evidence: Maker r2 presents “list defaults to most-recently-added first”; maker r3’s exhaustive map contains only “FR-014 order most-recent-first,” with no user-selectable sort task. Client r2 says “The plan sounds good,” and client r3 approves the task breakdown.
decisions.note: The scoped behavior fixes ordering to most-recent-first instead of allowing selection among sort keys. The client does not identify the missing sort control.
